s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive proximal muscle weakness with inflammatory and autoimmune features
salient_findings: Progressive proximal muscle weakness over 2 months
Morning stiffness of small hand joints
key_facts: 14-year-old girl presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness
Difficulty combing hair and rising from a chair
Became wheelchair-bound over weeks
Morning stiffness of both small hand joints lasting about 30 minutes
Dysphagia for solids and liquids
Poor appetite without fever or weight loss
History of thyroiditis in 2015
Family history of Prader-Willi syndrome in a younger sister
Symmetric muscle strength of 4/5 in upper limbs and 3/5 in lower limbs
Brisk reflexes more pronounced on the left
Tenderness at the fourth and fifth proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally
Leukopenia with WBC 2.96 × 10^3/µL
Microcytic anemia with hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL
Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Normal creatine kinase
Suppressed TSH and elevated free T4
Markedly elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies
Antinuclear antibody titer was 27
Bilateral sacroiliitis on MRI

shortlist.label: Juvenile Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Hashimoto Thyroiditis
shortlist.why_kept: History of thyroiditis, suppressed TSH, elevated free T4, and markedly elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and muscle weakness

shortlist.label: Autoimmune Myositis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies, antinuclear antibody titer, and muscle weakness

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive proximal muscle weakness, morning stiffness, and tenderness at the joints, along with elevated inflammatory markers and specific muscle strength findings, are most consistent with Juvenile Dermatomyositis. The presence of bilateral sacroiliitis on MRI also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hashimoto Thyroiditis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of thyroiditis and current thyroid function tests show suppressed TSH and elevated free T4, the primary symptoms and findings are more indicative of a muscle and joint condition rather than solely a thyroid condition.

rejected.label: Thyroid-Associated Myopathy
rejected.why: This condition does not fully explain the patient's joint symptoms and elevated inflammatory markers.

rejected.label: Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes Juvenile Dermatomyositis, but the specific diagnosis of Juvenile Dermatomyositis better explains the patient's symptoms and findings.

rejected.label: Autoimmune Myositis
rejected.why: This term is too broad and does not specifically capture the unique combination of muscle weakness, joint symptoms, and inflammatory findings in this patient.
